utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I meanwhile use the time for the following matter. It's a withdrawal of Defence motions. On the 8th of December of this year, the Defence filed a motion withdrawing its motions for admission of the evidence of Jojin Kljecanin, Bozo Davidovic, Bogoljub Kos, and Dragisa Serdar. In light of the Defence`s withdrawal of the evidence of Serdar and Davidovic, the Chamber hereby clarifies that D1276 and D1241 are marked not admitted. Could even deal briefly with another matter. It's about an exhibit number. During the number of Milos Kovac on 1st December document bearing 65 ter number 03797 was assigned to Exhibit P7741.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: However, the Registry attached the document to document P7742, and the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to reassign Rule 65 ter number 03797 to P7741 in e-court. Good morning, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll continue to hear your evidence, but I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic. And could I also inquire with the parties whether a time arrangement has been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not that we discussed, but I'll adjust.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Yes, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just to put on the record, Your Honours, with regard to the lists sent by the Defence yesterday morning, the Prosecution has reviewed and would agree to eight documents which we've sent to Mr. Lukic that can come in without Mr. Lukic having to go over them with the witness. We received a new list this morning with some additions it seems and we will review that as well and come back as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would read and I provided Your Honours with the list as well, and the Registrar. I don't know if you were given the list. If you have it in front of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a list before me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the tool to speed up, and it's -- it's mostly dealing with the second part of that breakthrough after Nova Kasaba, until that column reached the territory under control of AB and H. And I would open only three documents to summarise. It's those three documents on the second page, and then I will move to burials and exhumations. So just to have it on the record, I'll read the numbers, and on the list you have footnotes from the analysis of Mr. Pavlovic, so we'll propose to be admitted: 1D05879. We will ask to be marked for identification since it lacks translation 1D06272. Also to be marked for identification, 1D06273 and 1D06274. The following documents are translated and we would tender them into the evidence, and they are: 1D05083, 1D07247, 1D06275, 1D06259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't seem to have those figures which starts with a seven on my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know whether -- you provided us with an earlier list or whether the new list is there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have any starting with 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, you said 07.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- let me check. It's 1D06247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I'm at 1D06274, not 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under two rows below, you have this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 624 -- yes, that I see. Can you say your numbers against, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, apparently you have a list. Could you provide it such a way that we can check that during the break so as --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the list you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you -- you read a few numbers out of that list, and there are not very much in a -- in an order which made it easy for us to find them. If you write down just the numbers, I think there were some six or eight, write them down, if you have them, give them to Mr. Registrar. He'll either copy it or give it to us so that we can check it on our list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I misspoke. That's the list we have in front of us. There's nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a list consisting of three pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just entered them from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the help of Mr. Registrar, I think we'll resolve that. Let's -- let's -- let's first hear your questions and the answers. And the one you mentioned are the ones not opposed, not objected to by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When Mr. Lukic began reading there were some that we didn't oppose, the MFI ones obviously. But this other list that we got this morning, I'm not sure if Your Honours have it, there are more documents, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one list consisting of three pages and whether that dates from yesterday or from today I wouldn't know, because there's no date on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I might suggest, Mr. Lukic has from e-mail from us the ones that we do not object to from yesterday, from the list from yesterday morning and, thereafter, we can discuss this new list and we can put it to Your Honours in written form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that and let's try to resolve it and not use court time for it. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I read the rest of the numbers so the Prosecution knows exactly ... I'm afraid there might be some confusion. It will take two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is -- take you two minutes. It's your time, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the next one is 1D06275; then 1D06259; the next one 1D06264; next, 1D05888; next, 1D05889; next 1D06276; next, 1D06277; next, 1D06279 for identification, lacking translation; next, 1D06250 for identification, lacking translation; next, 1D06281 for identification, lacking translation; and the last one, 1D06282 for identification, lacking translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we've got your list. Of course, we don't know which ones are objected to. We'll hear that from the Prosecution later. Further, I see "Statement of," sometimes given to whom, sometimes not given to whom, so we do not know whether that's a statement prepared for ICTY purposes or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is not a single one on this list prepared by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's at least may remove any concerns about Rule 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bis or ter, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Bis or ter. Please proceed, for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Next I would call up to see it on our screens, 1D05890.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Um, sorry to interrupt. Your Honours, I wonder if we can go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavlovic, we can see that Lieutenant Selim Oriz [phoen] on 26th of July, 1995 gave a statement. I'll just going to show the last statement to you in order to speed things up although perhaps we should have seen some other excerpts. We need to look at page 67 in the B/C/S and page 11 in the English version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I can ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fourth paragraph from the bottom, it states: "In my opinion, we had our biggest losses in the Kamenica sector, when the column was cut off, and after that, panic among the combatants increased. I think much more could have been done in that respect, that we did not listen to those who came after us." And the last sentence in the document states: "I estimate that we lost at least 4 to 5.000 able-bodied men." I would like to show you another document now, 1D06280. It's a section of the transcript during the testimony of Mr. Butler in the case against General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to look at e-court page 67.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all extra microphones be switched off, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we should go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we shortly see 1D06281.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're looking at the book by Mr. Carl Bildt. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... seek to see page 88 in e-court. It's page 66 of the book. [Interpretation] In his book, Mr. Bildt, as we can see on page 66 of the book states the following: "[In English] And probably more than 4.000 people had lost their lives in a week of brutal ambushes and fighting in the forests, by the roadside and in the valleys between Srebrenica and the Tuzla district, as the column was trying to reach safety." [Interpretation] Do you know where Mr. Bildt was in 1994, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the point in time when the events in Srebrenica were unfolding in July 1995, Mr. Bildt, as far as I know, was the special peace envoy of the European Union to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Of course, the reason why I took his opinion as a reference point was because at that position he had insight into information -- intelligence data from the field from international representatives in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and he wrote that later in his book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what were his other positions in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after this period, he became the High Representative in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he participate in some conferences?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In particular, the Dayton Peace Conference. I think he took part there. In any case, he was someone who was well-informed in terms of intelligence and what was going on in the field, and he was at the highest level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would just propose into evidence cover page and this page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do so, a line before there it reads: "In five days of massacres, Mladic had arranged for the methodical execution of more than 3.000 men who had stayed behind and become prisoners of war." Is that something you gave authority to as well or just the yellow line -- the yellow highlighted portion? Because you explained how well-informed he was, so I'm wondering whether it's limited to the yellow portion or whether you would also rely on the other part I just read. Could you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- [Interpretation] I thought the question was for the Defence counsel. I quoted this part from his book regarding the circumstances I was dealing with and that is what I was discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer now my question. The question was whether you gave some authority to the knowledge and the ability of Mr. Bildt to know what had happened, whether you then also accept the previous few lines where he concluded, as I read, that Mladic had arranged for the methodical execution of more than 3.000 men who had stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I were tasked to deal with that particular portion, I would have to go through the same process when I analysed the losses during the breakthrough. I would have to collate all the relevant document, analyse them, put them in order in order to produce conclusions, which would require months, if not years, much as I did for my own analysis. I did not make conclusions based on a sole piece of information or document. We know what analytical work entails. Many documents, their cross-referencing, their analysis, and collation. As you could see, I took a large number into -- of documents into account. Perhaps I could have included more, if that was a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I did refer to the entire book. I did not try to steer clear of anything, in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that again was not my question. But the authority of Mr. Bildt in this respect, you say, I would have to verify that, and you didn't verify that on the others although, in general terms, you accept Mr. Bildt as someone who was knowledgeable about the events. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I was busy with the losses of the 28th Division sustained during the breakthrough. This is just one of many documents that I tried to cross-reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're evading an answer to my question. Whether you accept the authority of Mr. Bildt as such and whether you would accept it on a similar level for the previous lines. Not to say that he is necessarily right or wrong, but you praised his knowledgeability and whether that would -- if there's any reason not to accept that for the previous lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And, incidentally, that sentence that Judge Orie read also relates to losses during the same period in the same area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I may be of assistance. I did mention what Mr. Bildt's position at the time was. He had access to intelligence information for everything. However, I cannot comment upon the previous sentence because I did not include it in my analysis. As for the segment I was tasked with, I said, yes, he was in that position and he had access to information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I asked you whether that would be any less true for the previous sentence. I'm not -- I didn't ask you whether you agreed with him but whether there's any reason to less or even more accept his knowledge, his ability, to know what had happened in relation to the previous few lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I've answered, but I will repeat. In order for me to comment on any part of his book, I have to put together many documents concerning the topic, and I have to analyse them in order to produce some kind of assessment. As for the highlighted part, did I that, but I did not do that for the previous sentence. Otherwise, it would have been unprofessional, if I had done that. I cannot say if it is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you understand my point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I fully understand. I didn't even ask you whether it was correct or not. I asked you whether the same praising of his knowledgeability, whether there's any reason to believe that he was less knowledgeable on the part on the previous sentence, in view of his position, his access to intelligence, all the reasons you mentioned answering Mr. Lukic's questions, whether you -- there's any reason that you would give him less authority on other parts of the book.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said he had access to information in keeping with his position. That is not in dispute. It is as it is. What I did say was that I cannot comment on the previous part because I did not deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- he did have information, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was just as well-informed on any matter, not just the lines you focussed on. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only I would comment on this, Your Honour. Now, you are seeking the opinion of this witness on something he didn't deal and did you not permit to us seek his opinion on something he dealt with. I just want it on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, first of all, you're not supposed to comment on what I asked. You asked questions to this witness about the background of Mr. Bildt, his access to information and his knowledgeability. And that was put in general terms, not exclusively in relation to that. The questions what was his position did he have -- I asked whether there's any reason to believe that he would have been less knowledgeable on a portion of the book on which you did not focus but which I read to him, and I only did so after you had tendered the document. So I let -- I allowed you to ask all questions you wished to put to the witness. It was only when you tendered it that I asked this additional question. Mr. Registrar, the number for the book would be ... for the excerpt of the book.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1396, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were just hoping that the date of the book could come in as well. It's on page 5 [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you can agree on it, then we don't need page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the year when the book was published?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's 1998 from our reading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1998. No objections. Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I consult with the client for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can do so if he sticks to our rule that he should not speak at audible volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear Mr. Mladic's voice so ... No speaking aloud, Mr. Mladic. Last warning. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the meeting between Mr. Mladic and Mr. Bildt when they met in Dobanovci on the 14th of July, 1995 around the time when everything was going on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read hundreds of thousands of documents when I analysed all of it. Colloquially speaking, I may have touched upon it, but I wasn't particularly interested since it was not directly related to the topic. I do know there was a meeting. I think there were several people involved, including some senior internationals, but that's all I know, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us move onto the next topic. We will now deal with the part of the report that deals with the mortal remains of the killed members of the 28th Division of the Army of BH. I wanted to draw the Chamber's attention to P01557. It is General Ratko Mladic's order on returning things to normal in the municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would normally wait for my friend to pose the question but the Prosecution would object to the documents, the military documents which are -- in the English pages 48 to page 50 of the witness's report being shown to him and the witness commenting upon them. In the Prosecution's submission, it is outside the expertise of this witness to interpret military orders. I believe he also gives a reason with regard to infectious disease and epidemics as to the fate of these bodies. That is outside of his expertise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard from Mr. Pavlovic at the beginning of his testimony that his primary source in his work in the institute of missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and on today's job, today's position are military documents. The main issue of knowledge for his institute. He worked before, and for his office today. It's -- we have military documents tendered by the Prosecution through Ministry of Interior of Denmark written in Cyrillic that the witness said he she that did not have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- idea what that document is, and to say that gentleman cannot comment on military documents is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... first of all, a witness of fact is not an expert witness. You have presented this expert witness and given his credentials in terms of identification, exhumation and there was another, I think a third section. Now, you now say, Whatever is only indirectly related to that falls within his expertise as well. That's not true. I mean, the analysis of military documents usually requires an extensive military -- military expertise which is supported by the training, by the experience in the military field, et cetera, et cetera. Now, you haven't presented this witness as such. You have presented him as a witness in other fields. If this is what you think, you should have presented him as a military expert and then you could have told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, the first operative. First operative in that institute. Everything went through him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. I've seen persons who are first officers or even directors of hospitals. That doesn't make them doctors. Let's be clear on that. It's just a comparison. I leave it to that at this moment. Please proceed, but keep in mind, first of all, there's only an overall objection, that there's an objection. I have not ruled on that yet. With your questions, stay within the limits of the expertise of this witness and then please proceed. And you may put questions in such a way that you achieve your aim also by not relying on elements that are not within the scope of his expertise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just mentioned the first document, it's P exhibit, so I don't know what the objection is, whether it should be [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if you would have listened well, you would know what the objection was. Not to look at this document, but to put a certain type of questions, and Mr. MacDonald clearly explained that he did that unusually at this stage so as to be clear what he expects you to do, and I think the Chamber expects to you to stay within what we told you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 65 ter number from the Prosecution list 05794, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you deal with the fate of those who disappeared when you worked for the institute of missing persons in BiH?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those who went missing during the war in Bosnia or those who went missing who originated from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you rely on such documents as this one in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would not have been able to do our job had we not relied on military documents when it comes to those who went missing during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm the head of sector who deals with intelligence and analysis concerning the missing persons and the return of their remains to their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document before us is dated the 20th July 1995 from the command of the Drina Corps. We see here that asanacija or sanitation and hygiene measures of the battle-field are concerned. Under item 1, we find the following: "In co-operation with the civil defence organs, health centres and hospitals, the organs of public utilities enterprises and work organisations, and Ministries of Defence of municipalities, immediately organise and proceed with the complete clearing-up of the battle-field ..." What kind of information did you gather? Who took part in asanacija in terms of military and civilian authorities in the second part of July in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would have two objections to that question. Firstly, the who, if he is basing upon this order it would again be interpretation. Secondly, I think my friend referenced the word "battle-field" which, again, the Prosecution would submit requires a military interpretation for the area being talked about, which, again, outside the witness's expertise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you lay a foundation for your question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll then -- posed open question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That doesn't make the need to lay a foundation any less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work at the institute did anyone ever object to you relying on such documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible. It is one of our primary sources --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Irrelevant question. Mr. Lukic, please proceed. The question is not whether someone else objected to or did not rely on it. We want to know -- the laying of a foundation is not whether others commented on it. Witness, what, in terms of battle-fields, what is your definition of a battle-field and from where do you get that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not deal with military lexicon definitions. We were looking for those who went missing, and we took into account all documents that assisted us in the process, including, military ones. That was the context we worked in, and it involved intelligence and analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an answer to my question. Could you please put your next question to the witness, Mr. Lukic. Or perhaps I would have one. Witness, do you have any knowledge about who in military structures would be tasked with sanitacija [phoen] on the ground? And could you tell us on what basis you have knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clearly defined in this document who is to be involved. There are rules of service that existed on all sides. It was done by the bodies of civilian protection when ordered by the military structures. That is general knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's general knowledge, you say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is general knowledge when it comes to the work we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And those rules of service you are referring to as relevant, could you tell us which rules of service you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In what sense? Precisely? You want me to cite the documents and their numbers or something else? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please describe them for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rules of service define what asanacija in the battle-field is, and it is specified who is to be engaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then point at what rules of service would apply in this context, in the context of this document? Indeed, specifically rules so-and-so or ... And Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't necessary for me to deal with the details of rules of service. We had to know how it all worked in principle, and we can see it in this document. We can see who was included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To me, it was sufficient to be able to follow it all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that, that that's your opinion. You said sanitation was done by the bodies of civil protection when ordered by the military structures. Where is that relation between the military structures ordering --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Municipal? I talked about things how they were inherited from the JNA in principle. The same principle was adopted on all sides with variations. However in principle and depending on the situation, it was done by public utilities enterprises and the bodies of civilian protection, i.e., civilian authorities. To what extent any military bodies were included depended on each particular case. It was a chaotic state during the war and things were not all orderly in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What were the rules on the involvement of the military authorities in this respect? Should they order it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not go into such detail. We were interested in the principles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic, and please keep in mind what we said earlier about sticking to the expertise of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if I may just go to your question that started this debate. At page 22, line 1, you said, "Who took part in the asanacija in terms of military and civilian authorities in the second part of July 1995." This was after reading paragraph 1 of this document that's on the list -- that's on the screen by asking who. Do you want additional entities and people in addition to those mentioned in paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I wanted if this witness has knowledge how it worked in practice at that moment during his work, if he got any additional information who actually did work on the terrain in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you want his knowledge apart from what this order says?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah Your Honour. If it's really implemented in practice, if he got that information during his work. If he does not know, he can tell me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know. You go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, as part of your work at the institute, did you follow this lead? Did you try to find those who went missing, whether some of them were found on the ground and how many were buried?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a well-known fact, from my experience and that of my colleagues as well as on the basis of the analysis of the documents I read, that asanacija was always done in the period following a combat activity. And we can see that in orders such as this one, as well as the statements of those people who survived from the 28th Division. They could see asanacija being implemented in the field. We also have regular reports of VRS members who, for example, asked for additional fuel in order to be -- to bury enemy soldiers. Some of it was done after September 1995 during the joint work of the entity commissions. From 1996 to date, perhaps some 700-plus sets of bodily remains were exhumed, and I put together a list of some 660 people who were -- whose bodies were collected on the ground and identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. What was interpreted was that they were exhumed. Were they exhumed or ...

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were collected from the surface. They were cleared. So after that, there is the question in the context of this order and other information that I referred to, where the rest of the bodies were. I'm talking about thousands of bodies. And then here it is said that it is essential to complete asanacija because, at that time of the year, it was very hot and some diseases would break out and affect people and animals. So on the basis of reviewing documents and some samples, I came to the conclusion that these orders were carried out and that the asanacija was implemented and obviously some of those bodies that were part of this clearing of the terrain were buried in some mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 1D06282, please. 1D06282.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps before we look at that, perhaps we first take a break. But before we do that, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Witness. But before we do that, I saw, Mr. Lukic, that -- you may follow the usher. That what is uploaded from Carl Bildt's book at this moment is the entire book and, therefore ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to see with the Prosecution which parts they want uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- define the excerpts as soon as possible so that we can limit ourselves to a few pages rather than to 446. We take a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. With regard to the last answer of the witness, the Prosecution would consider that answer is outside of his expertise. We did not object because unfortunately we found the question did not necessarily elicit that answer. However, we appreciate that is now on the record. It was an area that we hadn't intended to cross on, but given that it's on the record now we consider that we consider the most efficient way forward would simply be to cross-examine the witness on that claim, Your Honour. The question I had in mind was Mr. Lukic stating: "Mr. Pavlovic, as part of your work at the institute, did you follow this lead, did you try to find those who went missing" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What page and what line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry. Temporary transcript 26, line 5, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness entered the courtroom while you were speaking. That doesn't cause you any problem from what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Although if there's to be further discussion on this, we would ask that it be outside the presence of the witness, but I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, one second. I must admit due to overlapping speakers I do not know whether I have a full recollection of what was said. But if you say you want to cross-examine the witness on that. If Mr. Lukic wants to make any comment you'd rather have it not in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Any further discussions right now, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further discussions. Mr. Lukic, if you want to further discuss the matter, then we have to ask the witness -- either to leave or at a later stage to leave at least before the start of the cross-examination. If you say, well, it's on the record. That's what will happen --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will discuss this, and, Your Honour, I would just remind that this witness was called as an expert in tracing, exhumation and identification. So tracing is what we were discussing here. He has to trace first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So apparently there's some dispute about whether it falls within the field of expertise yes or no. You consider it was. You've asked the question. The question has been answered. Despite your opinion, Mr. MacDonald, you say, you will cross-examine the witness on it. Fine. There seems to be no real problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will just recalled 1D06282 on our screens, please. This is not translated. And I will just read one short part of the statement. We need -- and this is statement of Suljic, Idriz from 30th November 1995. And if we can see page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavlovic, we're looking at paragraph 3 here, the big, long paragraph. Line 10 from the top of the paragraph it states the following: "While we were in Pobudje, we were watching from a hill as the Chetniks in Pervane were walking along the asphalt road and collecting bodies with a loader and loading them into a FAB truck. They were driving them towards the village of Kravica, municipality of Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... from D01379 which is federal Ministry of Defence, security and intelligence sector. We read that also 500 Bosniaks were driven by trucks in the same direction. We have P03518 that discusses the matter and we can find it in paragraph 70 of the work of Mr. -- footnote 70 of the work of Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavlovic, today you talked about the 700 that were collected from the surface, from the ground. And you're talking about your lowest assessment of 4.500 to 5.000 men who were killed during the attempt to break through?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. My friend has just referenced in his question the conclusion of the witness which Your Honours precisely stated was outside of his expertise the assessment of the number of people who died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. What we said about it is clear. Mr. Lukic, at this moment, refers to it. Let's leave it to that and nothing more, nothing less. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you and in your work, what was the conclusion that you reached about where those bodily remains are?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained in the previous session, and taking into account all the documents that I went through, and in view of my experience in this work, and on the basis of certain information and data, I reached the conclusion that a certain number of bodies of those killed, members of the 28th Division, during the breakthrough, were cleared when the terrain was being cleared after the combat actions. This is also stated in the order that we had the opportunity to see and that they were buried in certain graves --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name of the corps that the witness mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the corps you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Drina Corps. Assistant commander for logistics of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said in some graves. Which graves did you mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, according to the information that I found, it is my opinion that these bodies that were cleared from the terrain were buried in primary and secondary graves, as we refer to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will come to that, and we will look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that, I would like to tender document 65 ter 05794.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, do you have in mind any graves that were exhumed and were presented in the evidence of the Prosecution, or are you talking about other graves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned that in the overview, in the table that I submitted. These are graves that relate to the events in Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is, we have received evidence presented by the Prosecution about exhumation in mass graves, and there's quite some detail. People who were identified, who were found in those mass graves. When you're talking about these persons having been buried in graves, do you have the same graves in your mind so that they were found in those same graves, or do you have other graves in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not aware of exactly which graves were mentioned by the Prosecution. I followed the trail of my own information, and I presented that in the overview that I presented and that I assume you received. I did not deal with information about whether the Prosecution submitted something or not, but I think that this evidence is clear. I -- I did present them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me stop you there. The overview -- Apparently, Mr. Lukic, you understand what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 1D06331. We're just coming to that after we admit those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not yet for us. We haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, Judge Moloto asked one question. We just saw shortly that document. We are now going back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We never really got it. As I said to you the other day, we never got that document. And, you know, it's supposed to have been part of the report and that part of report we never got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We don't have it. That's one. Second, Witness, do I understand you well that you are not aware of the evidence presented to this Chamber in relation to exhumation of persons, all the evidence, and let's say in the Srebrenica area in 1995, you have no knowledge about what was presented as evidence to this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I said that I didn't know in detail what the Prosecution submitted to the Chamber, which graves these were. I didn't deal with that. I was just working on tracing where the bodies could be of the persons who were killed in the breakthrough. Those are the bodies that I was tracing. I was trying to find out where those bodies could be. And so I presented to you the evidence that I acquired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's move on. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sure you can answer the simple question: Which graves did you deal with? From which graves did you exhumed the people that you analysed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I submitted that in the material in the analysis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you've got to know what graves you went to analyse. We will look at the document when it comes, as Mr. Lukic has told us. He is getting to that. But can you answer the question right now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that we're not understanding each other. I'm talking about the manner in which I, in this segment, reached conclusions in my analytical process. I did not go and exhume anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These skeletons were already exhumed. If you permit me, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll get to that. I'm just a bit surprised that talking about large numbers of dead persons having been found in graves, that you cannot tell us whether these were graves which were exhumed by the Prosecution or through the intervention of the Prosecution, or whether these were exhumations done separately by your people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is something that I can't answer. I'm sorry, forgive me. Perhaps I misunderstood. All the mass graves, primary and secondary graves, linked to the events in and around Srebrenica in July 1995 were exhumed either by the Prosecutor's office, I assume, or by the authorised prosecutor's offices in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is clear. No one else could have been performing these exhumations from these graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I analysed the data from those exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the exhumations not performed by your own people but performed by the Prosecution or those instructed by the Prosecution to do so. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Members in my sector took part in the exhumation, each exhumation is an investigative action under the jurisdiction of a specific prosecutor's office, so pursuant to international agreements, we are present during the exhumation process from start to finish. But for specific segments of our work, we use certain sectors. For intelligence aspects of our works, we use the intelligence institutions. For information from exhumations, we co-operate with the prosecutor's offices, and so on and so forth. And this is something that is ongoing until the bodies are handed back to the family members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. MacDonald, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. With regard to 1D06331, that is the list that Mr. Lukic briefly showed I believe on Monday and plans to proceed to, the witness stated that he provided it with material with his report. We received that list on Sunday evening at 5.30, Your Honours, and we have yet to receive the majority of the supporting documentation underlying it. And I was going to bring this up when Mr. Lukic moved to that list, but seeing as the witness has claimed, I believe, he provided it with the material with his analysis, we didn't get it till Sunday, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it seems to be pretty relevant to know what the witness in this respect presented, because I went through his report searching, for example, for the word mass or mass graves, et cetera and then you hardly find any concrete information. But apparently there is a list unknown to us, although presented by the witness. Let's move on and let's wait for what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can also tell you the concern of Mr. MacDonald, he asked me whether I have statements that support this list I'm going through just in few moments, and I said that Mr. Pavlovic brought some statements, but it was too late to put them in the record and I couldn't ask him since I could not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you receive the list? That's first. The second support for that list maybe have come late. When did you receive that list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic provided that list to us when he came here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The list of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 6331. We uploaded as Mr. MacDonald just told us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you said you expect us to know about that list. When did you provide that list to the Prosecution, the list, the attachment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hmm?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the Defence, yes. When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that you knew about the document because, on Monday, you had it in front of you. I brought it with me, and I gave it to the Defence as an overview of specific examples on the basis of which I reached certain conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you didn't bother to do that when you presented the report? To the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be honest, I am not quite versed in all the procedures that have to do with your work, so I am in this situation for the first time. I must say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but in your work, didn't you see that as part of your work as a person who is going to -- who specialising in tracing, exhumation and identification of people who lost their lives in war? Didn't you think we need to know who you have identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're probably right. But there was some objective circumstances. To be honest, I didn't even know till the last day whether I would be coming to testify at all. I mean, there was some confusion about whether I would testify or not. Now, I was informed a day or two before. I had no idea that I would actually be coming to testify. There were many things that were unclear, at least as far as I'm concerned. I'm not really somebody who is familiar with this process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because -- excuse me. Because these are working overviews that I used. And I showed that to the Defence when I was speaking with the Defence counsel. I wanted to explain to them how I came to certain conclusions. This was during preparation for testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't think that these were necessary for the court to see. You say you don't understand how we work, and I don't understand how you've bothered to have this list, if you didn't see it as part of your work. If you saw it as part of your work, I don't know why you didn't make it part of your report. You see my problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I offered for admission 05794.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That Exhibit D1397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the next one, 1D06282.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections either. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D1398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1398 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we would move to this one, 1D06331. Maybe it's easier if we only go through English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the document in front of us, the English version of the document. Who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted this overview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I discussed with my friend I think this document should not be broadcast [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought only on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's page 5, actually, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You have apparently considered what could be broadcast and what not. Please stay on the safe side, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did we get the answer? Yes, yes, you said that you drafted the document. What is this document? What does it show?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document gives an overview of specific examples that led me to assess and to conclude that the large number of bodies of casualties of the breakthrough of the 28th Division, which is referred to in military analysis on the Bosniak side, also based on eye-witness reports, media reports, and also scientific research of the actions of the 28th Division, as well as testimonies of family members and combatants, so I tried, pursuant to my own work description, to work out where these bodies could have ended up, and this is a kind of overview of all the examples of certain members of the 28th Division indicating where their bodies were cleared from the terrain and possibly where they were buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was interpreted that these are all of the cases. Did you include all of them or were these just some kind of samples?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this is just an excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's -- it's just some examples, is what the witness said. It's not excerpts. It's not all the examples. Some examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're not there to do the interpretation. If there's any doubt about it, you know how to deal with that. You say these are examples. How many disputed cases do you have in total?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not enumerate them here. I just mentioned some examples that I could. I don't know exactly. We can count them. In any case, it raises some concern or creates some doubt that I used to follow the lead and, if necessary, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I was, first of all, interested in -- if you say, These are examples. First of all, how many examples do we have in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, for the first category of arguments, I mention only two or three examples. For the second category, perhaps ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many in total in this document, I asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not count them. I'm sorry. We can count them now? It wasn't important to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if you say examples, then it's -- it's some out of a total. How many cases in total you had reason to dispute; that's one. But before you answer that question, could you tell what was the dispute? I mean, what makes it disputed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this: I mentioned the categories of argument as I defined them. The first set of arguments and examples includes people who are still missing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stop you there. Where do we find exactly in this document, if we find it in this document, the set of arguments? Or is it in your report? And if it is in your report, where is it in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stop you there. Where in this report do we find this first group or first set of examples? Where do we have them? On ...

utterances.text: Then I go back to my first question. What is then in dispute about these remains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no dispute. Perhaps only weeks after the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in dispute with what exactly? I mean, apparently you have developed some thoughts on how these bodily remains ended up at certain places. Are you opposing any other thoughts? Are you opposing conclusions drawn by others on those bodily remains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the title of the document, we can't find -- no, I see it says "disputed." Yes. Maybe I added the title later. What I wanted to mention were the examples that in the course of my work may have served as an indication in -- about where some bodily remains ended. There's no dispute from point of view. I'm simply trying to find the people who went missing during the breakthrough. I was just trying to show that some of those people were collected from the surface as part of the asanacija process and later buried in certain mass graves. There is no dispute, per se.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no dispute, although you used that in the title. Well, at least it's now clear that there is no dispute. These are just cases where you thought that specific attention should be paid to the details in order to find out how and -- how they may have died. Is that ... under what circumstances. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These examples prove that there was asanacija after combat and that these people were then buried in mass graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's three steps further. But I leave it to Mr. Lukic to further ask questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before he does, what you've just said, sir, about that they prove that there was asanacija after combat and these people were then buried in mass graves, was that the objective your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The objective of my report is to analyse the losses during the breakthrough of the 28th Division and the fate of the mortal remains of those who perished, i.e., where they ended up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where they ended up that was the objective: To find where they ended up. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Where did you get your information from, the information you entered in this document?

utterances.text: I referred to the examinations of bone samples.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me continue. So bone samples concerning all the exhumations done so far, primarily by the ICMP. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that some bodies were found on the surface while others may have been found partially on the surface and partially in mass graves. Let us look at page 2 of this document. You mentioned Tisova Kosa. Let's look at the last name on the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not the same as I -- yeah, yeah, we have it. The last name on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please explain this entry so that I don't put questions to you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see that the body of this person was collected at Tisova Kosa as part of asanacija. We also have the bone sample number. It is TIS 1 and so on. That information comes from the ICMP report in 2013 that was forwarded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, it says, "removed as part of sanitation of the terrain on location Tisova Kosa what's the basis for that knowledge? It doesn't say what the source of that information is. Could you tell us on what basis you make this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you find this person in the specific database I just mentioned, you will see that in the ICMP database it stated that the person was found at the two locations, as I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But you said it was part of a sanitation of terrain. Does is say in the ICMP this was sanitation of the terrain and there -- and how did they establish that it was sanitation of the terrain, rather than just finding parts of a body there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, I'm sorry. Of course, I consulted other databases with respect to where people were found. At the institute we do have an overview of where people were found. When discussing asanacija, some people, their bodily remains were found in two or three different places because the bones were dispersed and then there are people whose remains can be found in a number of different graves. We have all that information for the people, the location of Tisova Kosa means that they were collected from the ground on the surface. It can easily be checked and verified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You certainly are aware that whether people are found as a result of sanitation of the terrain or in any other context is a -- seems to be a rather important matter in this case. Where do you find that this body, apart from being found in Tisova Kosa, that it was found during the sanitation of terrain; and if so, sanitation of the terrain by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Asanacija and exhumation was done by the acting prosecutor's offices at the point in time on orders from the prosecutors who were in charge. As part of the forensic team, there is -- there's a pathologist who marks every bone sample --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me stop you there. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This part of the skeleton was found as part of asanacija after 1996. It is obvious that somebody was collecting the bodies on the surface and buried them because some of them were, indeed, collected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it now at least becomes a bit clear to me where the word "asanacija" is often used in a totally different context, and I take it that you're aware of that. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They are not receiving translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, there is no translation. Okay. Could we just check. Yes, it's there again. Are you aware that asanacija is often used in evidence as a reference to the armed forces clearing up the terrain after combat situations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I also discussed that type of asanacija after combat. Perhaps I may have been unclear, but when I mention it here, it involves forensic investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's now is the specific problem here, apart from that parts of the bodies were found in two different locations? What -- I mean, that happened often as we have heard. What's now the specific problem here? Because you said it proves something. What does it prove?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In examples such as this, where some remains were found on the surface as part of asanacija by the acting prosecutor's office, whereas another part of the same person was found in a mass grave may indicate or may lead us to suppose that asanacija was done after combat, as foreseen by the order we saw stemming from the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well -- let me just re-read what you now said. One second, please. You are telling us that this indicates that this was the type of asanacija stemming from the Drina Corps order. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

At the same time, other parts of the same person were found in a mass grave elsewhere as part of another asanacija. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 6 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And cross-examine the person properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this material, I mean, this apparently is something of substance rather than that who is biased and who is doing wrong, et cetera, this is a -- and that material was only received two days does not clearly appear in the report. utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 7 of the document.

utterances.text: I would agree but I think Your Honours asked about where the different groups in this list are and there don't appear to be any, so I don't understand.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer that question by Mr. Lukic. I already started answering. utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the documents from the final identification of this person and while reviewing the certificate of death that is signed by the pathologist in the investigation, I saw that the injuries the person sustained were of -- were caused by explosives and, as a result of that, it seemed to point me in the direction of -- well, I know from the operational sense, I know that the 28th Division was shelled, they ran into mines, and they were also committing suicide by using grenades so these would be possible injuries sustained by those means. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does that prove apart from that we haven't seen the -- the post-mortem? At least I'm not aware of it. What does it prove? It's -- you suggest, I think, that he must have died in a combat situation where explosives were used. Could it be any other environment where explosives were used? I mean, what's your conclusion? Apart from that a person which apparently died from explosive -- I don't know yet, shrapnel or other things. He was found in a mass grave. That's apparently the facts you rely on. What does that tell us? More than what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I mentioned, I relied on witness statements and ABiH military documents. It is clear from those sources that the 28th Division was exposed to heavy artillery shelling. They came upon minefields and committed suicide; in certain cases by hand grenade. That is why I found it interesting, given the context and that there is a possibility, in addition to other evidence I mentioned, that this, too, could lead us to the assumption that after combat there was asanacija and that people were buried in mass graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But could you exclude that explosives were used in other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of this specific location, I can't say anything. I'm simply trying to raise an issue, open up a possibility. I did not draw a conclusion. There is a possibility that would be in keeping with some other sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now better understand. Mr. Lukic, those materials, are they available? Because you point at a specific example, so I take it that you have reviewed the underlying documentation. Apart from the format of this part of the report being totally different from what we saw before, any explanation for that to be elicited from the witness? Witness, we see numbers; not sequential. We see all kind of information. That's quite different from what we saw in the beginning. What explains the difference in format between the beginning of this report and the present portion we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it a question for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] As I said already, this was a kind of overview of mine of certain examples that I forwarded to the Defence, and this is how they decided to present it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand that the Defence has created these green lines, et cetera, totally different from these first part of these examples, and if what is the case I'd like to know. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We merged those two documents into one. That's what we did but we didn't put this green --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where does this material come from? Let's say on from page 8 where the different format starts and of which we see now the first page, page 8 to 12, I think, or perhaps even 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... which is a totally different format. Could you tell us where you got that from? Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I created this overview, and, in principle, there were two different formats, but the issue on hand is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The numbers we start with, that is, the very -- the grave-site number, where is that taken from and what does it present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see -- I'm sorry. This is basic information about each location. It's a kind of overview. As I was going through everything, I was creating a sort of an outline or overview for me to find things more easily. That is what I relied on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was talking about numbers. I see that the first entry bears number 281; the second is 286; the third is 288. That at least suggests that there was a list with sequential numbers. Is it taken from any other list? What do these numbers stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I copied it from different sources. I can't recall exactly what the figures stand for precisely. The number is unimportant to me specifically. There's no reason for me to deal with it. What was important to me for my work were the co-ordinates the exhumation dates, locations, designation of location, that is what was important for my work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it may -- if we are in these kind of numbers, it suggests that there were over 200 and even goes far beyond that. Numbers of grave-sites, is that a mass grave-site, is that an individual grave? Because I see that the co-ordinates are quite different as well. As far as I can see now, none of them corresponds with another, which suggests a lot of graves and that may be relevant for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The co-ordinates describe particular locations and they have to vary from location to location. When discussing specific events there were many exhumations and asanacija exercises.

utterances.text: Witness, sometimes if you have a mass grave the co-ordinate would be the same, isn't it. You would have a lot of bodies in exactly the same location. Yes. Okay.
