utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we go to the right of the table, you will see the type of grave. Is it a mass grave, individual grave, is it asanacija, meaning on the surface. But we need to go to the right of the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do so. Because we'd like to understand what is presented to us as evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's good. Each line describes a location, and it is stated whether it is a primary or secondary mass grave or is it part of asanacija. Every line stands for one location, and it also includes some of my comments with regard to specific locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "every line," which line are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lines from left to right. I'm not discussing columns. I'm discussing the lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see two columns. One is MG, mass grave; and the next column is type of grave. Now, the mass grave, there are numbers with it. What do these numbers stand for? For the number of dead people found there or -- what -- what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the total number of bodies and parts of bodies found in a specific mass grave, be it primary or secondary, as we can see in the next column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which seems to suggest that there were a lot of different mass graves dealt with here. Because we have all different numbers, 1 -- 288, 224, 242, 200, 305, 244. These are all different mass graves then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you have a complete list of mass graves which were considered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see here the mass graves that were encompassed in my work. It doesn't mean they are all here, and it does not include such locations where mortal remains were found on the ground. This is just a portion that was important to me for what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was: Do you have a complete list of mass graves which you considered? Do you know how many mass graves you -- you looked at, you considered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the list more or less, the one I dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did deal with a full list of all mass or individual graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is not the question. The question is the full list of the graves that you looked at, that you investigated, not the full list of graves, of mass graves, but the list of those that you considered. These ones, how many are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The list is before us. This is the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we move a little bit to the left, further to the left of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To the left. Not to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to go to the beginning of this page. Yeah. That's here. Here. Here. Here. Now if you look at the heading in red, it says grave-site number. Now, my -- from that, I read and I thought you explained that earlier, that the 281 is the number of the grave. Is that what you said? At some stage you said it didn't mean anything to you, but then you later said it was the number of the grave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the number of location chronologically, either of a mass grave or a location where bodies were found on the surface. That's all. It was unimportant to me. What was important to me was to have the location, the date, what was found --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you are explaining something that I'm not asking. Let me ask. We see on this page, the highest number is 344. Assuming that that is -- I'm just making an assumption that is the highest number of these graves here. Is it -- does it mean that, in fact, you saw 344 -- or there were 344 graves around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are discussing the topic or theme of my work, I did, say, 200 exhumations per day. In the course of my work, over 700 were performed there were many exhumations an examples of asanacija. So those figures are great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But a great number of people can be found in one grave. I'm not talking about the number of people exhumed. I am not talking about the number of graves from where exhumations took place. I'm asking: Should we accept that the number of graves, whether they are mass graves or single graves, goes up to 344.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Are you discussing a specific event or are you talking about exhumations in general in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not about a specific, I'm not asking about exhumations. I'm talking about the number of graves out of which exhumations took place. I'm saying is it your evidence that right through the war the number of various graves that can be associated does go as far as 344, possibly more because you didn't investigate all of them. So 344 would be the number of graves the heading says grave-site number. So number of the grave-site, that's what the heading says, and I'm saying: Were there 344 grave-sites?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were many grave-sites, many more than 344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've answered my question. That's all I've been asking for, for all this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could I, a bit on the same subject. Could we move slightly further to the right. Yes, there we are. That's what I need. We see one column, type of grave. On the first entry, it says: Secondary mass grave and the line before that, it says MG, mass grave, and gives a number. You told us that that is the number of bodies exhumed from that mass grave. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask you to move just a little further to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is good. Thank you. It actually represents examples from the fourth group, as I refer to it, that I found interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- as can you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you mind to answer my question. 288, did I well understand that, for the first entry, that 288 is the number of persons exhumed from that mass grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the total number. We are discussing the column before the column where we see secondary mass grave. So 288. It's the total number of bodies and bodily parts exhumed from that specific mass grave. So full bodies and parts of bodies. And then I classified it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So these classifications are done by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked on the column entitled: Complete bodies. I checked that and I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you check it or did you establish it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived at these figures by checking the documents I had at my disposal, which I have already referenced. I can explain what it means and what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I now slowly start seeing what the document is about. Took me a while but that's perhaps I'm a bit slow. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just for the record to say that again the Prosecution was unaware these were two different reports, nor had the Defence formatted them, nor have we the underlying material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's hereby on the record. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned the fourth category. Please explain what you wanted to say. We already dealt with the first three. What would be the fourth?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In trying to trace the bodies of those who perished in the breakthrough, what struck me as illogical was that there was a certain number of complete bodies in graves defined as secondary mass graves. In keeping with our practice and based on my experience in the sector and that of my colleagues, it was illogical to have such high numbers of complete bodies in secondary graves, because those bodies are usually dug up by construction machinery and put on a truck and then unloaded from the truck into the next grave after a certain period of time. So there should have been decay of tissue and dispersion, literally put. The bodies must have fallen apart to a certain extent, and that raised issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think no one asked the picture to be moved. Could we go back to where we were. Yes. So you're surprised by the number of complete bodies in the secondary mass graves. Let's have a look at entry number 1, yes, we leave it to that secondary mass grave, complete bodies 50, body parts 238. For the second, could you explain what body parts there means because you said 224 was the number of bodies exhumed. Complete bodies, 224. And apparently some 47 other things remained there as well. Do you know what that stands for, 47 cases BP or RAV01-?-? What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we're talking about a primary grave at Ravnice Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we'll move onto the next one. It's the secondary grave at entry number 3. Twenty-six complete bodies, where 242 were exhumed. Next item, secondary mass grave 59 complete bodies. Next one, secondary mass grave out of 305, 9 complete bodies. Next entry, 79 complete bodies out of 244. You say you were surprised by the number because you would expect body parts to fall off. If I read this, most of the bodies were incomplete and only a very limited number anywhere between -- I would say anywhere between 5 and 25 or 30 per cent were complete bodies. What did then surprise you so much about these numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If a body part found in a mass grave doesn't mean it's an entity in and of itself. As you can see, if you look at the fourth secondary mass grave, 200 were exhumed, 200 complete body parts, out of those, there were 59 complete bodies and 98 entities arrived from the location in total. It means that a number of different body parts can represent a single entity. If we look at the sixth example of Kamenica Cancari 02; 244 was the total of remains exhumed. Out of that 79 complete bodies, 165 body parts and out of that, 113 were identified. In other words, body parts -- a number of body parts usually means that they may belong to a single set of bones so out of 113 total identified there were 79 complete bodies, and the rest of these identities were arrived at based on the study of the body parts assembled rather than complete bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although it's not an answer to my question, I noticed that where you earlier said that the number in the column mass grave with a number was bodies exhumed and you apparently now are telling me, which perhaps may be very logical that it's not bodies exhumed from that, but that it could be bodies or body parts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do, in this column where you say ID total, you call that entities. What do you mean by entities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually I meant to say identity. Identity of a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does -- I do understand that that's then -- how many individuals with distinct features could be established on the basis of what was found in a mass grave; for example, by identification through DNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you think the job is finished after producing this table?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are simply some of my observations based on experience and expertise. I raised issues. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You attended these exhumations.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Did you see what kind of machinery was used?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, they were loaders with a fork --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you said this is a list which must be used to continue searching for the person. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In that specific case, yes. All I said was that all the persons were there who were killed in the breakthrough, in combat and everybody else is there as well. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.text: We were just considering how to proceed, Mr. MacDonald. The first question is whether we'd try to finish the cross-examination of this witness today which seems not to be feasible. utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

At this point, though, I cannot say whether I found the statements in the documents that I received from the Defence. I assume that that was so for the majority of the cases and then also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever you brought to The Hague, are you willing to share that with the Chamber and you give it to the Victims and Witness Section? utterances.text: Yes. They certainly will be in touch with you. It's highly appreciated that you want to do it immediately that the Prosecution has sufficient time to further review those materials. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, also if Mr. Pavlovic used any database apart from our database maybe, I don't know, what he used, maybe something -- it's something from other organisations. Maybe he should be instructed to share that with Your Honours as well.

utterances.text: Yes. I thought that was included in my instructions but to avoid any lack of clarity. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may now follow the usher. I hope that you feel better soon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll use the time to deal with a few matters on the agenda. The Chamber always tries to have an empty agenda before we go for longer periods of recess. In order to avoid any misunderstanding when I announced an extended session prior to that we had explored to that extent that was possible at all, and, again, we found great co-operation by those assisting us in this courtroom. I'll start with a first item dealing with final trial briefs. Last week, the parties made submissions in court in relation to the final trial briefs. The Chamber grants the parties' request to fix the word limit to 300.000 words. In relation to timing, the Chamber considers that it is still too early to address how many weeks or months after future events the final briefs should be filed. There are a number of Defence witnesses remaining, the Chamber may take some time to decide on all evidentiary matters prior to closing the Defence case. There will be a rebuttal and possible rejoinder case and the Chamber may require some time finally to close the entire case with the filing of the last evidentiary decision. The Chamber has taken note of the parties' submissions but maintains that any periods of non-sitting, for example, this coming January, must also be used by the parties for its final brief preparations. The Chamber will not grant an extended period of time after the close of the case for the preparation of final briefs, especially if the parties had various opportunities to prepare prior to the closure. I move onto my next item, and we move into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Next item deals with documents used with Yasushi Akashi. During Akashi's testimony on the 23 and 24th of November, exhibit numbers were reserved for a number of documents pending the Prosecution uploading excerpts. The Prosecution informed the Defence and the Chamber via an e-mail on the 26th of November that the excerpts had been uploaded into e-court. The Defence has not objected. In light of this, the Chamber instructs the Registry to carry out the following changes: 1. Replace P7692 with the B/C/S excerpt and corresponding English translation uploaded into e-court as Rule 65 ter number 11148a. 2. Replace P7693 with the excerpted pages uploaded into e-court as Rule 65 ter number 02393a. 3. Attach the excerpted pages uploaded into e-court as Rule 65 ter number 04472a to P7704. P7692, P7693, and P7704 are hereby admitted into evidence. Next item still deals with associated exhibits related to the same witness. On 23 November the Defence stated that it would try, at the end of the witness's testimony, to reduce the number of associated exhibits tendered pursuant to Yasushi Akashi's Rule 92 ter motion. This can be found at transcript pages 41679 through 682. Ultimately, there was insufficient time to give the Defence the opportunity to do so in court. The Chamber hereby gives the Defence one week to make submissions on this matter. Next item deals with P7541 tendered through Radoje Vojvodic. On the 8th of September of this year, P7541, a list of military observers, was marked for identification, pending the provision of an English translation. This can be found at transcript page 38837. On the 10th of December, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that an English translation has been uploaded under doc ID 0687-4507-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach this translation to the original and admits P7541 into evidence. Should the Defence dispute the translation, it may inform the Prosecution and the Chamber within a week, but should then submit the document to CLSS for verification. Next item is an oral decision on the admission of P7449 through P7453 all tendered through expert witness Ewa Tabeau on 2 July 2015 during the reopening of the Prosecution's case in-chief. In relation to P7449 through P7453, Tabeau's proof of death report for Tomasica, the corrigendum to the report, the annexes to the report, an addendum to the report, and a PowerPoint presentation of the report, the Defence submits that it does not have access to Tabeau's "keys" matching victims and therefore the report's methodology is up clear. This can be found at transcript pages 36879 to 36881. The Defence also submits at transcript page 36879 that the: "...numerous errors in the report and the perceived bias of the witness do not render the report to be of an expert such that it would assist the Chamber." Furthermore, in relation to P7453, the PowerPoint presentation, the Defence argues that to the extent it provides additional information beyond that contained in the report, such information was not provided in a timely manner in accordance Rule 94 bis, since it was only provided to the Defence on 30th of June 2015, just days before the witness testified. These submissions can be found on transcript page 36883. In response, the Prosecution submits that P7453, the PowerPoint presentation is merely a exemplification of the report to facilitate the presentation of Tabeau's evidence in court and that while it includes some corrections to the report, those corrections were already included in P7450 which is the corrigendum. These submissions can be found on transcript page 36884. In relation to the "keys": The Prosecution submits that the methodology is clearly spelled out in the report and also refers to it included in previous reports already admitted into evidence. This submission can be found at transcript page 36880. The Chamber recalls that the applicable law for the admission of evidence is set out in Rule 89(C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which allows a chamber to admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value. Although Rule 94 bis does not provide specific guide-lines on the admissibility of expert evidence, the jurisprudence has established the following requirements for the admissibility of an expert report: The proposed witness is qualified as an expert, the expert report is relevant and of probative value, and the content of the expert report falls within the accepted expertise of the expert witness. The Chamber notes its decisions of the 7th of November, 2013 and the 24th of February, 2015 recognizing Tabeau as an expert in the field of demographics and statistics more generally, and that the proof of death report for Tomasica and the related documents fall within the scope of her expertise. The Chamber finds that Tabeau's proof of death report for Tomasica and the related documents are relevant because they relate directly to the re-opening of the Prosecution's case - namely, exhumation of the Tomasica grave-site. In relation to the Defence submissions about not having access to Tabeau's "keys" and that the reports methodology is unclear, the Chamber notes that the report's methodology is set out in section 2 of the report and therefore this submission is unsubstantiated. Further, the Chamber understands that the Prosecution had offered previously to make these "keys" available once they had been recreated. This can be found at transcript page 36880. To the extent that the Prosecution has not made these "keys" available to the Defence as to today's date, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to make them available to the Defence at its earliest possible convenience. With regard to the Defence submissions concerning errors and bias, the Chamber does not exclude the possibility that errors and elements that could be perceived as expressions of bias could reach a level so as to deprive an expert report of its probative value. The Chamber has admitted expert reports in this case that contain some errors and were not always entirely free from elements that could be perceived as expressions of bias. In its evaluation of the expert reports, as with all evidence, the Chamber will consider such errors and elements when assessing the weight to be accorded to the evidence. The Defence has not demonstrated that the errors and alleged bias reach such a level so as to deprive the relevant documents of their probative value. The Chamber therefore finds that Tabeau's proof of death report and the related documents have probative value and are admissible pursuant to Rule 89(C) of the Rules. The Chamber considers P7453, the PowerPoint presentation of the report, to be a demonstrative exhibit only and therefore finds that the Defence concerns in relation to the timing of its disclosure and its content are without merit. Therefore, the Chamber considers that P7449 through P7453 meet the standards of admission pursuant to Rules 89(C) and 94 bis of the Rules and admitted them into evidence. P7451 and P7452 are to remain under seal. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I now move on to the Rule 92 bis attestation for the redacted statement of Witness Miroslav Homa. On 18 November, the Chamber conditionally admitted Miroslav Homa's redacted Rule 92 bis statement, pending the filing of the attestation and declaration. On 19 November the Chamber noted that the unredacted witness statement had been uploaded into e-court, and requested that the Defence upload or release the redacted witness statement. The redacted statement and required attestation and declaration have since been uploaded under doc ID 1D29-0168. The Chamber instructs the Registry to replace D1360 with the newly uploaded documents and hereby admits D1360 into evidence. I now move to excerpts of documents used with Milos Kovic. During the testimony of Milos Kovic on 30th of November and the 1st of December, P7724 was marked for identification, while P7723, P7742, P7743 and P7752 were reserved, all of which were pending excerpts to be uploaded into e-court. On the 9th, the 11th and the 14th of December, the Prosecution, via e-mail, informed Chamber and Defence that it had uploaded into e-court revised versions of the relevant documents bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 07617a, 03580a, 07871a, 02368a, and 19650a respectively and requested replacement and admission of all aforementioned revised excerpts. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace P7723, P7724, P7742, P7743, and P7752 with the excerpts uploaded into e-court and admits them into evidence. The Defence has no objection to the admission of P7752 and has one week to revisit the four other documents. I now move to excerpts of documents used with Mitar Kovac and Milos Kovic. During the testimony of Mitar Kovac and Milos Kovic on the 19th of November and 30th of November, excerpts of documents bearing Rule 65 ter number 33442 were put to the witnesses. The document was tendered through Milos Kovic and P7718 was reserved for excerpts to be uploaded into e-court. On 11th of December, the Prosecution via e-mail informed the Chamber and the Defence that the relevant excerpts had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 33442b. The Chamber instructs the Registry to replace P7718 with the newly uploaded excerpts and admits it into evidence. The Defence has one week to revisit the matter. I now move to the remaining issue from the testimony of Ostoja Marjanovic, P7624. On 9th November, this number was reserved for excerpts of document bearing Rule 65 ter number 33385 which is the transcript of the witness, Ostoja Marjanovic's prior interview with the Prosecution. This can be found at transcript page 40996. On 11 December, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and Defence via e-mail that the excerpts had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 33385b. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign P7624 to these excerpts and admits into evidence and the Defence has one week to revisit the matter. A few remaining issues from the testimony of Mile Dosenovic. D1195. On the 13th of August, 2015, D1195, a radio intercept was marked for identification, under seal, pending English translation. On the 28th of October, the Defence advised via e-mail that the translation had been uploaded under doc ID 1D26-3907. The Prosecution responded, confirming that it did not object to the translation. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translation to D1195 and admits D1195 into evidence under seal. D1196. On the 13th of August, D1196, a map, was marked for identification, under seal. On the 30th of October, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that it does not object to its admission but that the map is already in evidence as part of D1200. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to mark D1196 as not admitted. P7499. On the 17th of August, P7499, a military document, was marked for identification pending the verification of its translation. On the 30th of October, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that a revised translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0051-0433-1-ET. The Defence responded on the 3rd of November confirming that it did not object to the revised translation, and the Chamber hereby therefore instructs the Registry to replace the translation of P7499 with the revised one and admits P7499 into evidence.
